questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.
The little boy cried with pain when he burnt his fingers
questions.solution:
A) 'No substitution required' होगा क्योंकि "when he burnt his fingers" का अर्थ है जब उसने अपनी उंगलियों को जलाया। जबकि 'As he burning his fingers' का अर्थ सही नहीं है क्योंकि यह phrase grammatically रूप से गलत है, 'When he burns his fingers' present tense को सूचित करता है जो इस संदर्भ में सही नहीं है, और 'While he burn his fingers' भी grammatically रूप से गलत है।
'No substitution required' should be selected because "when he burnt his fingers" correctly conveys the meaning of the boy crying out in pain when he burnt his fingers. Whereas, 'As he burning his fingers' is grammatically incorrect, 'When he burns his fingers' indicates present tense which is not appropriate here, and 'While he burn his fingers' is also grammatically incorrect.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
This is best book for children to read.
questions.solution:
C) 'Best'के बदले'the best'का प्रयोग होगा क्योंकि 'best' से पहले 'the' का उपयोग करना आवश्यक है जब यह superlative degree में होता है; जैसे— This is the best book for children to read.
'the best'will be used instead of 'best' because it is necessary to use 'the' before 'best' when it is in the superlative degree; Like— This is the best book for children to read.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Rahul had strong pain in his stomach
questions.solution:
D) 'strong'के बदले'severe'का प्रयोग होगा क्योंकि जब हम दर्द की तीव्रता का वर्णन करते हैं तो 'severe' का प्रयोग किया जाता है; जैसे— She had severe headaches last night.
'severe'will be used instead of 'strong' because when describing the intensity of pain, 'severe' is used; Like— She had severe headaches last night.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
The skunk had a conspicuous spinal stripe.
questions.solution:
'A) conspicuous'के बदले'noticeable'का प्रयोग होगा क्योंकि 'conspicuous' का अर्थ 'easily seen or noticed' होता है और 'noticeable' भी यही अर्थ रखता है; जैसे— The skunk had a noticeable spinal stripe.
'noticeable'will be used instead of 'conspicuous' because 'conspicuous' means 'easily seen or noticed' and 'noticeable' also means the same; Like— The skunk had a noticeable spinal stripe.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.
It is a general belief that the female ostrich guard the nest at night
options: 3) does guard the nest in night
4) is guarding the nest at night.
questions.solution:
B) ‘guard'के बदले 'guards' का प्रयोग होगा क्योंकि 'female ostrich' एक Singular Subject है और Present Simple Tense में Singular Subject के साथ Verb में 's' या 'es' का प्रयोग होता है; जैसे— The sun rises in the east.
'guards the nest'will be used instead of 'guard the nest' because 'female ostrich' is a Singular Subject and in Present Simple Tense, we use 's' or 'es' with the verb for a Singular Subject; Like— The sun rises in the east.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
The road which connecting the two states is overcrowded
questions.solution:
A) Connecting'के बदले'connects'का प्रयोग होगा क्योंकि 'which' Relative Clause में verb का simple present tense में होना चाहिए; जैसे— The road which connects the two states is overcrowded.
'connects'will be used instead of 'connecting' because in 'which' Relative Clause the verb should be in simple present tense; Like— The road which connects the two states is overcrowded.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
As I have no time to discuss the points, so I wrote a email to her.
options: 1) so I wrote a e-mail to her
2) so I wrote an e-mail for her
3) I wrote an email to her
4) I write an email to her
questions.solution: C) 'So'should not be used here because 'As I have no time to discuss the points' already provides the reason, and using 'so' makes it redundant.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can replace the bracketed word segment in the following sentence.
Children should avoid giving out personal details online (which will) identify them or their location
questions.solution:
C) which will'के बदले'that could'का प्रयोग होगा क्योंकि Relative Clause में संभवना दर्शाने के लिए Modal Verb 'could' का प्रयोग उचित है; जैसे— It was Ram, Laxman and Sita who went to the forest.
'that could' will be used instead of 'which will' because in Relative Clause, the use of the Modal Verb 'could' is appropriate to show possibility; Like— It was Ram, Laxman and Sita who went to the forest.

questions.question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.
This win could enhance to be a historic turning point in the fortunes of the team.
questions.solution:
D) 'Prove'काप्रयोगहोगाक्योंकि"prove"काअर्थहोताहैकिसीतथ्यकोसाबितकरनायाप्रमाणितकरना।जबकि'Demonstrate'काअर्थहैप्रदर्शनकरना, 'Confirm'काअर्थहैपुष्टिकरना,और'Accomplish'काअर्थहैप्राप्तकरना,जोइससंदर्भमेंसहीनहींहै।
'Prove' should be used because it means to demonstrate the truth or existence of something by evidence or argument. Whereas, 'Demonstrate' means to show or display, 'Confirm' means to verify, and 'Accomplish' implies achieving something, which don't fit in this context.

questions.question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.
Mothers have great animosity for their children
questions.solution:
'A) animosity'के बदले'affection'का प्रयोग होगा क्योंकि 'animosity' का अर्थ शत्रुता या बैर होता है जबकि माताओं को अपने बच्चों के प्रति प्रेम होता है; जैसे— Mothers have great affection for their children.
'affection'will be used instead of 'animosity' because 'animosity' means hostility or enmity, whereas mothers have love for their children; Like— Mothers have great affection for their children.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Sonam’s cat used to chase the mouse into the kitchen and knock through a tower of pots and pans.
options: 1) knock out a tower of pots
2) knock over a tower of pots
3) knock inside a tower of pots
4) knock away a tower of pots
questions.solution:
'B)'knock over a tower of pots'होगा क्योंकि जब कोई चीज किसी वस्तु से टकराकर उसे गिरा देती है, तो 'knock over' का प्रयोग किया जाता है; जैसे— The wind knocked over the fence.
knock over a tower of pots' will be used because when something hits an object and causes it to fall, 'knock over' is used; Like— The wind knocked over the fence.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement required’.
I am so glad that I ran into you on the way.
questions.solution:
B) 'No improvement required' होगा क्योंकि "ran into" का अर्थ है संयोगवश किसी से मिलना। जबकि 'Ran over' का अर्थ है वाहन द्वारा कुचलना, 'Ran away' का अर्थ है भाग जाना, और 'Ran out of' का अर्थ है किसी चीज का समाप्त हो जाना, जो इस संदर्भ में सही नहीं है।
'No improvement required' should be selected because "ran into" means to meet someone by chance. Whereas, 'Ran over' means to drive over something, 'Ran away' means to escape or flee, and 'Ran out of' implies depleting a supply of something, which don't fit in this context.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Dhruv’s anger blazed of uncontrollably
questions.solution:
D)'blazed'के बदले 'blazed up' का प्रयोग होगा क्योंकि 'blazed' के साथ 'up' का प्रयोग होता है जो अचानक और तीव्र रूप से उभरने का संकेत देता है; जैसे—His anger blazed up uncontrollably.
Blaze up(phrasal verb) – to suddenly become very angry भड़कना
'blazed up' will be used instead of 'blazed' because 'blazed' is commonly paired with 'up' to indicate a sudden and intense emergence; Like—His anger blazed up uncontrollably.

questions.question:
Select the option that will most suitably substitute the underlined part of the given sentence.
He was not happy until he gave up his job and live as a fakir in the forests
options: 1) until he gave up his job and lives
2) until he gave up his job and lived
3) unless he gave up his job and lives
4) until he gives up his job and lived
questions.solution:
B) lives के बदले 'lived' का प्रयोग होगा क्योंकि 'was' Past Tense में है और उसी Clause में दूसरी भाग में Verb 'lives' भी Past Tense में होगी; जैसे— He was not happy until he gave up his job and lived as a fakir in the forests.
‘Lived’ will be used instead of 'lives' because the verb 'was' is in Past Tense, so the other verb 'lives' in the same clause will also be in Past Tense; Like— He was not happy until he gave up his job and lived as a fakir in the forests.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.
The company do not broke the law at any time.
questions.solution:
D) 'do not broke' के बदले 'does not break' का प्रयोग होगा क्योंकि 'Do/Does/Did + Base form of verb' का प्रयोग होता है, अत: शेष विकल्पों को सरलता से हटा सकते हैं और अंतिम विकल्प D का चयन कर सकते हैं; जैसे— The company does not break the law at any time
'does not break' will be used instead of 'do not broke' because 'Do/Does/Did + Base form of verb' is used, so we can easily eliminate the other options and select the last option D; Like— The company does not break the law at any time.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.
The plum tree in our garden is cover in blossoms, as are the trees outside my office window
questions.solution:
A)'is cover in'केबदले'is covered in'काप्रयोगहोगाक्योंकियहPassive Voiceकावाक्यहैऔरPassive VoiceमेंVerbकाPast Participle Formप्रयोगहोताहै;जैसे— The plum tree in our garden is covered in blossoms.
'is covered in' will be used instead of 'is cover in' because this is a sentence in the Passive Voice, and in Passive Voice, the Past Participle form of the verb is used; Like— The plum tree in our garden is covered in blossoms.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
We feel warm on the subject
questions.solution:
A) 'warm on' के बदले 'warmly about' का प्रयोग होगा क्योंकि Verb को Modify करने के लिए Adverb 'warmly' की need है; जैसे— We feel warmly about the subject.
'warmly about' will be used instead of 'warm on' because to modify a verb, the adverb 'warmly' is required; Like— We feel warmly about the subject.
